Hi team —

Acme shared an initial redline (attached) and a populated order form. They asked us to confirm a few items before we send back our first-pass comments:

- Confirm party legal names and billing entity (they listed “Acme Integrations, Inc.” but procurement uses “Acme Integrations LLC”).
- Residency / data processing region: they want EU residency for a subset of customers — need to confirm if Redwood Private or Hosted with EU region is required.
- Request for a lower indemnity cap and carveouts for open-source dependencies (their counsel will propose exceptions).
- Clarify SLA credits and a stricter uptime definition in Exhibit B.

Attachments: Acme_MSA_Draft_v1.docx, OrderForm-SeatSchedule.xlsx, ExhibitA-Customer-Contacts.xlsx

Timeline: Acme hopes to finalize commercial terms by the end of next week (May 28). They are flexible on start date, but procurement needs a PO and approved MSA before provisioning.

Can legal advise on (a) acceptable party name wording, (b) whether we can require Hosted EU region for the subset (and any pricing implications), and (c) our stance on indemnity cap language and OSS carveouts for a customer of this size?

Thanks — I can run a short sync with Acme if that helps.

Best,

Thanks Rafael — quick read and initial thoughts below. I’ll do a formal first-pass redline once we confirm the party and residency details.

1) Party name / billing: we need the counterparty’s legal entity as appears on invoices. If Acme prefers LLC vs Inc, we’ll mirror the entity on the signature block and Exhibit A (billing contact). Please ask them to confirm the exact EIN and remit-to address.

2) Residency / Data Processing:
- If they require EU-only hosting for a subset of customers, we can support via Redwood Private deployed to EU region, or Hosted with an EU model pinned to region. That will impact pricing (addendum for data residency).
- Request sample dataset/volume for the EU workload so we can size capacity.

3) Indemnity / Cap:
- Their proposed unlimited carveouts for OSS are risky. We usually accept OSS carveouts limited to license compliance issues; we push for a single-digit multiple of fees as cap (unless enterprise requires higher).
- Suggest we propose a counter: cap = aggregate fees for 12 months, with mutual carveouts for gross negligence/willful misconduct.

4) SLA / Exhibit B:
- Need to map their uptime language to our standard credit schedule. If they want stricter definitions, we can offer a premium SLA at Dedicated tier — will require procurement sign-off.

Please have Ben or procurement answer: (A) exact legal name/EIN; (B) whether EU residency is mandatory or optional; (C) expected monthly token volume for the EU subset.

I’ll prep a redline with comment tags for these open items.

—Kimberly Park
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
(Attachment stub: none)
